final_boundary_decision.text: Agent states it will cut from the start of “Yeah,” to the start of “Right”

official_result_aggregate.other_checks: completed and passed per previously archived aggregate report; no private detail accessed here

direct_evidence: Scribe JSON provides word/spacing entries with start/end, speaker_id and logprob; punctuation is embedded in text; it has no explicit hesitation/event tag.

Agent identified the hesitation phrase from transcript text, then explicitly selected the start of “Yeah,” through the start of “Right”; the selected cut removes the whole restart phrase plus the following 0.56s spacing reported by transcript.

Agent generated a timeline with waveform and transcript, viewed that PNG via view_image, viewed source frames, then viewed before/after output images. This establishes image inspection, not listening or audio-semantic understanding.

EDL retained ranges meet cuts.json at the same seconds after ms-to-s conversion. The render call used that EDL and the source-spec/no-enhancement switches; no evidence of a time-base conversion or helper changing the boundaries.

The sole nonzero command was timeline_view with unsupported --start/--end/--interval options (exit 2). Agent read --help, retried positional times, generated and viewed the timeline image. This is an Agent argument-selection error; no general helper defect is evidenced.
The official aggregate says the cut-range check failed; it does not identify a boundary side, offset, or the correct time.
reasonable_but_unproven: Phrase-level deletion may have treated a potentially meaningful short acknowledgment as part of the disfluency; logs establish the whole phrase was selected, not that this semantic choice caused the score failure.
Scribe word timestamps may drift from acoustic onset/offset; no local forced alignment or acoustic boundary ground truth was collected.
The official temporal tolerance or annotation convention may be narrow; this run does not disclose or establish the tolerance.
unknown: Which edge (or both) failed, by how much, and the official tolerance.
Exact acoustic onset/offset of the hesitation and whether the short acknowledgment should be retained.
Whether a human listening review or a validated audio-capable model would select different boundaries.
diagnosis.primary_classification: Agent selection strategy / insufficient verified audio-semantic evidence; timestamp precision and official tolerance remain candidate factors. No evidence that render time conversion altered the chosen cut.
diagnosis.next_capability: Improve the boundary decision protocol first. Existing Scribe transcript, timeline_view waveform/frame context, FFmpeg and render helper are reusable. If spoken meaning cannot be judged from transcript and waveform, separately validate an authorized listening/audio-understanding capability. Forced alignment can refine word timing but cannot decide which semantic material to remove.
diagnosis.budget: No evidence this was wall-time constrained: the Agent completed normally within its allotted phase. Do not increase budget based on this run.

limitations: No oracle, golden, private scorer files, target boundary, or inferred error was used for boundary diagnosis.
No new audio interpretation experiment was run.
